newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM denies influence peddling.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM denies influence peddling.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, responding to a Belgian newspaper report on a thwarted corruption investigation by a public sector supervision body, on Monday denied allegations of influence peddling.
"The Prime Minister has never directly or indirectly intervened in any investigation by the organisation," Dehaene's office said in a statement.

The Dutch-language newspaper De Morgen said Willy Vermeulen, the deputy director general of the Supervisory High Council, a semi-independent body fighting white-collar crime in the public sector, had been banned from leading a search for evidence in Dehaene's offices in 1992.
The paper said Vermeulen made the allegation in a report to selected members of the Senate Commission on Organised Crime.
It said the search was supervised by an official who had "good relations" with Dehaene's office.

De Morgen said the search was for evidence that bribes had been paid in connection with a contract for rat extermination on waterways signed at the end of the 1980s by the Transport Ministry, which was led by Dehaene at the time.
